label: Location and Spread on Metric Spaces
notes: This chapter, printed pages 21 through 35, replaces the Euclidean mean with a notion that lives on any metric space. We minimize expected squared distance instead of adding coordinates, so the same definition will later serve curved shape spaces where vector averages make no sense at all.

label: The Frechet Function
notes: The Frechet function measures, for each candidate location, the average squared distance to the random point. It is the metric-space stand-in for the variance functional, defined entirely through the distance rho without referring to charts, tangent vectors, or any linear structure on the underlying space.

label: Frechet Mean and Total Variance
notes: The Frechet mean is the set of points where the Frechet function attains its minimum, and the minimum value is the total Frechet variance. Because the minimizer may not be unique, we speak of a mean set rather than a single mean point throughout this chapter.

label: Empirical Frechet Mean
notes: Replacing the population expectation with an average over observed sample points gives the empirical Frechet function. Its minimizers form the sample Frechet mean set, the estimator we actually compute. Everything reduces to minimizing one scalar objective built from pairwise squared distances among data and candidates.

label: Existence on Metric Spaces
notes: On a complete and suitably bounded metric space the Frechet function is lower semicontinuous and proper, so its infimum is attained and the mean set is nonempty and compact. Existence is therefore cheap; it is uniqueness that demands the geometric work in the next slides.

label: When the Mean Is a Set
notes: Symmetry of the distribution against the curvature of the space can leave several equally good minimizers. The uniform law on a circle is the canonical warning: every point ties for minimum Frechet value, so the mean set is the whole circle rather than any single representative location.

label: Karcher Means: Local Minimizers
notes: Karcher means relax the global minimum to any local minimizer of the Frechet function. They are easier to find by gradient descent and often unique nearby, but a Karcher mean need not be a Frechet mean, so the distinction matters when reporting a location estimate.

label: Strong Consistency
notes: The Ziezold and Bhattacharya-Patrangenaru theorems guarantee that the sample Frechet mean set shrinks into the population mean set almost surely as the sample size grows. Consistency holds even when the limit is a set, with set-valued convergence measured by how far sample minimizers can stray.

label: A Central Limit Theorem
notes: When the population Frechet mean is a unique interior point and the function is smooth there, the recentered sample mean is asymptotically normal. The Hessian of the Frechet function and a distance-gradient covariance combine in a sandwich form that controls the limiting Gaussian fluctuations.

label: Sample Mean Convergence
notes: As we draw more points from a distribution concentrated away from symmetry, the empirical Frechet mean settles toward the single population minimizer. The visual shows the estimate tightening with growing n, illustrating the consistency statement that the earlier slide proved abstractly for general spaces.

label: Computing and Checking
notes: In practice we minimize the empirical Frechet function numerically and audit it with bootstrap resampling. Bootstrap bands on the circle reveal whether the estimated mean is stable or whether near-symmetry has spread the location across a wide arc, flagging an unreliable single-point summary.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We built location and spread from distance alone: Frechet function, mean set, total variance, the Karcher relaxation, and the consistency plus central limit asymptotics. The next chapters specialize this machinery to manifolds and shape spaces where the metric carries genuine curvature and quotient structure.
